gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Creative Pebble Pro's and Pebble X Plus's USB-PD port is power only and carries no audio. The higher outputs (Pebble Pro 30 W RMS, Pebble X Plus 30 W RMS / 60 W peak) need a 30 W+ PD adapter that is sold separately. All four Creative picks ChatGPT showed (Pebble V3, Pebble Pro, Pebble X Plus, T60) list SBC as their only Bluetooth codec, and the Edifier M60's LDAC is specified for Android 8.0+ sources.
standout_why: I compared against stackandvalue.com (cited). It states the Pebble Pro gives 'up to 10W RMS' from a standard USB port and 'up to 30W RMS' with a '30W USB PD adapter (sold separately)'. It does not say the PD port carries no audio, and it gives no Bluetooth codec for any pick. I could not read the text of the other cited pages: TechRadar, Tom's Guide (roundup and Pebble Pro review), Tom's Hardware and PC Gamer came back truncated after the title. So I cannot rule out that one of them states the codec or PD-port limits. That is why this scores 2 and not 3.
decides: This confirms the advice ChatGPT gave in both chats to use wired USB-C on a PC. Over Bluetooth, every Creative pick runs SBC (the only codec they list), and the M60's LDAC is specified only for Android 8.0+ sources. The finding also adds a wiring rule ChatGPT left out. A Pebble Pro or Pebble X Plus buyer who adds the 30 W PD adapter for full power still needs a second connection for sound: USB-C to the PC, Bluetooth, or AUX. The Pebble V3 must stay USB-powered even in Bluetooth mode. The Pebble Pro stays the value pick for a PC with a USB-C port, since Creative rates 10 W RMS from a 10 W USB-C port. The T60 and M60 have no such power-source caveat on the pages I read, and the T60 ships with its own 18 V 2 A AC adapter.
